## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

## Objective
- Build and finish a complete, playable 3D pixel-art survival-horror game titled “Ape Project” in the current repo from a prior failed/truncated attempt.

## Requirements
- 15×15 m subterranean lab lobby with metallic walls, industrial floor, lab racks, beakers, terminals.
- Four hydraulic security doors with animated weighted open/close cycles and interactive switches on the left side of each door frame.
- 500×500 m slightly hilly, sparsely treed jungle exterior.
- Lethal-Ape-inspired ape player with upright walk, quadrupedal sprint, crouch, hill traversal, and first/third-person camera.
- Blind auditory apex predator “Mossman”: 2.8 m tall, moss-green/dark-striped, eyeless, wide mouth, 33 km/h top speed, halved turning agility, acoustic tracking of footsteps/running/hydraulic doors.
- High-fidelity 3D pixel-art presentation, dynamic lighting, particles, procedural assets, no flat sprites or realistic high-poly assets.
- User asks not to ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (≤1280 px wide) and read only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Use static HTML plus vendored Three.js modules so the runtime start script can serve it without a bundler.
- Present 3D at reduced internal resolution with CSS `image-rendering: pixelated`, nearest-filtered procedural textures, flat-shaded low-poly/voxel geometry.
- Use a three-core collection loop: recover 3 isotope cores from jungle beacon sites, return to lab terminal, trigger emergency lift, step on pad to win.
- Add exterior hydraulic release switches so players cannot be permanently trapped outside.
- Add procedural WebAudio, throwable rocks for decoys, medkits, datapad lore, rain/lightning, fireflies, HUD, pause/note/death/win overlays, and mobile touch controls.
- Use `location.reload()` for restart/retry to avoid implementing full scene teardown.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected prior checkpoint/conversation: no game source existed; prior run only saved config and a truncated issue request.
- Vendored `three@0.170.0`, `BufferGeometryUtils`, and local Silkscreen/Share Tech Mono fonts.
- Created `index.html` with import map, HUD, start/pause/note/death/win overlays, and mobile controls.
- Created `styles.css` with full visual design, responsive/mobile layouts, effects, and overlay styling.
- Created `src/textures.js` with procedural canvas textures, signs, labels, and glow sprites.
- Created `src/audio.js` with synthesized ambience, footsteps, monster roar/steps, doors, pickups, alarms, thunder support, heartbeat, and win/death cues.
- Created `src/world.js` with lab, hydraulic doors, props, console, lift, terrain, jungle trees/ferns/rocks, core sites, medkits, notes, fireflies, collision, and interactables.
- Created `src/player.js` with ape model, locomotion/crouch/quadruped animation, stamina, health, noise, headlamp, collisions, and view modes.
- Created `src/monster.js` with large mossy eyeless model, acoustic state machine, inertia-limited turning, attacks, roars, spore trail, and threat output.
- Created `src/effects.js` with particle bursts, spores, dust, steam, sparks, rain, and indoor motes.
- Created `src/main.js` integrating renderer, scene, input, pointer lock, camera, HUD/compass, interactions, rocks, objectives, ascent sequence, mobile controls, and end states.

2. Check browser console/page errors and fix all module/import/runtime issues.
3. Capture desktop and mobile screenshots; verify gameplay starts, lab renders, HUD/compass are visible, and touch controls appear.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

import sys, zlib, struct, math

def read_png(path):
    data=open(path,'rb').read()
    assert data[:8]==b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    pos=8; w=h=bd=ct=None; idat=b''
    while pos<len(data):
        ln=struct.unpack('>I',data[pos:pos+4])[0]; typ=data[pos+4:pos+8]; chunk=data[pos+8:pos+8+ln]; pos+=12+ln
        if typ==b'IHDR':
            w,h,bd,ct,comp,filt,inter=struct.unpack('>IIBBBBB',chunk)
        elif typ==b'IDAT': idat+=chunk
        elif typ==b'IEND': break
    raw=zlib.decompress(idat)
    ch={0:1,2:3,3:1,4:2,6:4}[ct]
    bpp=ch
    stride=w*bpp
    out=bytearray(h*stride)
    prev=bytearray(stride)
    p=0
    for y in range(h):
        f=raw[p]; p+=1
        line=bytearray(raw[p:p+stride]); p+=stride
        if f==1:
            for i in range(bpp,stride): line[i]=(line[i]+line[i-bpp])&255
        elif f==2:
            for i in range(stride): line[i]=(line[i]+prev[i])&255
        elif f==3:
            for i in range(stride): line[i]=(line[i]+((line[i-bpp] if i>=bpp else 0)+prev[i])//2)&255
        elif f==4:
            for i in range(stride):
                a=line[i-bpp] if i>=bpp else 0; b=prev[i]; c=prev[i-bpp] if i>=bpp else 0
                pp=a+b-c; pa=abs(pp-a); pb=abs(pp-b); pc=abs(pp-c)
                pr=a if (pa<=pb and pa<=pc) else (b if pb<=pc else c)
                line[i]=(line[i]+pr)&255
        out[y*stride:(y+1)*stride]=line
        prev=line
    return w,h,ch,bytes(out)

def main(path, crop=None, cols=100):
    w,h,ch,px=read_png(path)
    if crop:
        x0,y0,x1,y1=crop
        # bounds in pixels fractions? absolute
    else:
        x0,y0,x1,y1=0,0,w,h
    cw=x1-x0; chh=y1-y0
    rows=max(1,int(cols*chh/cw*0.46))
    print(f'IMAGE {w}x{h} crop {cw}x{chh} grid {cols}x{rows}')
    lum_chars=' .:-=+*#%@'
    grid=[]
    for gy in range(rows):
        row=''
        for gx in range(cols):
            ax0=x0+gx*cw//cols; ax1=x0+(gx+1)*cw//cols
            ay0=y0+gy*chh//rows; ay1=y0+(gy+1)*chh//rows
            r=g=b=n=0
            for y in range(ay0,ay1,max(1,(ay1-ay0)//3)):
                base=(y*w+x0)*ch
                for x in range(ax0,ax1,max(1,(ax1-ax0)//3)):
                    i=y*w*ch+x*ch
                    r+=px[i]; g+=px[i+1]; b+=px[i+2]; n+=1
            if n==0: n=1
            r//=n; g//=n; b//=n
            lum=(r*0.2126+g*0.7152+b*0.0722)/255
            row+=lum_chars[min(len(lum_chars)-1,int(lum*len(lum_chars)))]
        grid.append(row)
    print('\n'.join(grid))
    # color stats
    cats={}
    for y in range(y0,y1,4):
        for x in range(x0,x1,4):
            i=y*w*ch+x*ch; r,g,b=px[i],px[i+1],px[i+2]
            mx=max(r,g,b); mn=min(r,g,b)
            key='black' if mx<18 else ('dark' if mx<45 else ('green' if g>=r and g>=b else ('cyan' if b>g*1.15 and g>r else ('orange' if r>g*1.25 else ('gray' if mx-mn<20 else 'other')))))
            cats[key]=cats.get(key,0)+1
    tot=sum(cats.values())
    print('COLORS', {k:f'{v*100/tot:.1f}%' for k,v in sorted(cats.items(),key=lambda kv:-kv[1])})
    # top quantized colors
    q={}
    for y in range(y0,y1,3):
        for x in range(x0,x1,3):
            i=y*w*ch+x*ch; r,g,b=px[i],px[i+1],px[i+2]
            k=(r//32*32,g//32*32,b//32*32); q[k]=q.get(k,0)+1
    print('TOP', sorted(q.items(),key=lambda kv:-kv[1])[:10])

if __name__=='__main__':
    crop=None
    if len(sys.argv)>2:
        crop=tuple(map(int,sys.argv[2].split(',')))
    main(sys.argv[1],crop)
EOF

## Objective
- Build and finish a complete, playable 3D pixel-art survival-horror game titled “Ape Project” in the current repo.

## Requirements
- 15×15 m subterranean lab lobby with metallic walls, industrial floor, lab racks/beakers, terminals, and four hydraulic doors with weighted open/close cycles.
- Tactile door switches on the left of each interior and exterior door frame.
- 500×500 m slightly hilly, sparsely treed jungle exterior.
- Lethal-Ape-inspired ape player: upright walk, quadrupedal sprint, crouch, hill traversal, first/third-person cameras.
- Blind auditory apex predator “Mossman”: 2.8 m tall, moss-green/dark-striped, eyeless, wide mouth, 33 km/h, halved turning agility, tracks footsteps/running/hydraulic doors.
- High-fidelity 3D pixel-art presentation, dynamic lighting, particles, procedural assets; avoid flat 2D sprites and realistic high-poly assets.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, ≤1280 px wide, and read only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Static HTML plus vendored Three.js modules, so the default static runtime works without a bundler.
- Render at reduced internal resolution with CSS `image-rendering: pixelated`, nearest-filtered procedural textures, and flat-shaded low-poly/voxel geometry.
- Three-core objective loop: recover 3 isotope cores from jungle beacon sites, return to the lab terminal, trigger ascent, then use the centre pad to win.
- Exterior hydraulic release switches prevent permanent trapping outside.
- Procedural WebAudio, throwable rocks, medkits, datapads, rain/lightning, fireflies, HUD, pause/note/death/win overlays, and mobile touch controls.
- `location.reload()` handles restart/retry to avoid full scene teardown.
- Brightness raised to exposure `2.4` with stronger lab/hemisphere/moon lights and lower fog density for gameplay visibility.
- Monster model normalized to exactly 2.8 m tall, feet aligned to terrain; player feet similarly aligned.
- HUD raised to `z-index:30` so mobile HUD buttons sit above the full-screen look pad.
- Use Playwright/DOM/scene introspection and pixel statistics for verification because the current model cannot ingest images.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented all core game systems across `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `src/*.js`.
- Fixed vendored addon import path to `../vendor/addons/BufferGeometryUtils.js`.
- Fixed keyboard input: `this.keys` is a `Set` and now uses `has`/`add`/`delete`.
- Added inline favicon to eliminate the prior 404.
- Fixed monster duplicate arm creation and duplicate spotlight scene insertion.
- Raised lighting/exposure and verified lab, jungle, beacon, and monster screenshots render non-black scenes.
- Verified start flow, walking, sprint/quadruped blend, crouch, pause/resume, all door switches, door collision blocking/opening, exterior release, notes, medkit, rock throw, monster hearing/attack, core pickup, locked terminal, ascent start/ready, lift win, and death overlay.
- Verified mobile touch layout: no horizontal overflow, joystick movement, run/crouch/view/lamp/throw/jump buttons, pause/resume, and death flow.
- Saved JPEG checks in ignored `screenshots/`: `desktop-title.jpg`, `desktop-lab.jpg`, `desktop-beacon.jpg`, `desktop-mossman.jpg`, `desktop-win.jpg`, `mobile-title.jpg`, `mobile-lab.jpg`.

### Active
- Fix repeated WebAudio page errors from the latest screenshot run: `Failed to execute 'setTargetAtTime' on 'AudioParam': The provided float value is non-finite.`
- Re-run strict desktop/mobile capture after the audio fix and confirm zero page errors/HTTP failures.
- Update `README.md` with game description/controls, then commit and push the currently uncommitted game.

### Blocked
- None known.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `src/audio.js` for every `setTargetAtTime` call and sanitize all frequency/gain/time arguments to finite values.
2. Re-run `/tmp/opencode/full-test.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/mobile-test.mjs`, and `/tmp/opencode/physics-test.mjs`; fix any regressions.
3. Run `CAPTURE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000/ CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/opencode/shots CAPTURE_STRICT=1 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs"` and confirm clean output.
4. Regenerate the JPEG screenshots after the audio fix; keep widths ≤1280 px.
5. Update `README.md` with the game overview and controls.
6. Commit all source/assets and push branch `opencode/42003146234`; report assumptions, controls, and final verification.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: app shell, HUD, overlays, import map, inline favicon.
- `styles.css`: full UI, responsive/mobile layout, HUD/mobile-control stacking.
- `src/main.js`: game loop, input, camera, HUD/compass, interactions, rocks, objectives, ascent, end states.
- `src/world.js`: lab, doors/switches, props, console, lift, terrain, jungle, cores, medkits, notes, collision.
- `src/player.js`: ape model, locomotion/crouch/quadruped animation, stamina, health, noise, headlamp, cameras.
- `src/monster.js`: 2.8 m Mossman rig, acoustic AI, turning resistance, attacks, roars, spores, threat output.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural audio; current source of non-finite `setTargetAtTime` errors.
- `src/effects.js`: particles, spores, dust, steam, sparks, rain, indoor motes.
- `src/textures.js`: procedural pixel textures, signs, labels, glow sprites.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js r170.
- `vendor/addons/BufferGeometryUtils.js`: geometry merge helper.
- `assets/fonts/`: local Silkscreen and Share Tech Mono fonts.
- `README.md`: still generic OMGithub boilerplate; game section pending.
- `screenshots/`: ignored JPEG verification captures.

## Important Context
- All game files are currently uncommitted on branch `opencode/42003146234`.
- `APP_PORT=3000`; the running server is started via `node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`.
- Default capture requires `CAPTURE_URL`, `CAPTURE_DIR`; strict mode is `CAPTURE_STRICT=1`.
- Capture auto-start matches only buttons whose accessible name is exactly `start`, `play`, `start game`, or `start now`; `#startBtn` intentionally uses `aria-label="Play"`.
- Headless software rendering runs slowly; `dt` is clamped to `.05`, so door timers and acceleration appear slow in tests. Do not treat that alone as a gameplay bug.
- Audio errors appeared only in the final screenshot run and remain unresolved.
- Current render stats are roughly 259–274 draw calls and ~69k triangles.
- `src/monster.js` normalizes the rig with a wrapper group to 2.8 m and offsets feet to the ground.
- `src/player.js` wraps the model to align feet and uses an eye height of `2.02 - crouch * .34`.
- Key tuned lighting values: exposure `2.4`, lab lights `44`, hemisphere `.85`, ambient `.65`, moon `1.6`, fog density `.0095`.
- Screenshots are saved in ignored `screenshots/`; image reading is unavailable to the current model, so visual checks use pixel statistics and scene/DOM assertions.

# APE PROJECT — Laboratory Escape

A complete, playable 3D pixel-art survival-horror game that runs in the browser with no build step.

You are the last ape in a failed subterranean research lab. Three isotope cores are scattered across the Mossline jungle outside. Recover them, feed the main terminal, and ride the emergency lift out — while a blind, 2.8 m acoustic apex predator called **Moss.Man** maps the world by sound.

## Play

Open the project through OMGithub, or serve the folder with any static web server and open `index.html`:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3000
# then visit http://localhost:3000/
```

A local server is required because the game uses ES modules and a vendored Three.js import map.

## Objective

1. Leave the 15 × 15 m lab through one of four hydraulic doors.
2. Follow the three columns of light to the isotope beacon sites in the 500 × 500 m jungle.
3. Pick up each core with **E**.
4. Return to the lab terminal and activate the emergency ascent.
5. Wait for the shaft to pressurise, then step onto the centre lift pad to escape.

The main terminal stays locked until all three cores are installed. An exterior release switch is mounted to the left of every door frame, so you can always get back inside.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard / Mouse |
| --- | --- |
| Move | **W A S D** or arrow keys |
| Look | Move the mouse (click the game to capture the pointer), or drag |
| Sprint / knuckle-walk | Hold **Shift** |
| Crouch / quiet movement | **C** (toggle) |
| Jump | **Space** |
| Interact / use switch / pick up | **E** |
| Throw a stone | **Q** |
| Toggle headlamp | **F** |
| Toggle first / third person | **V** |
| Pause | **P** or **Esc** |
| Toggle audio | **M** |
| Restart after death or win | **R** |

On touch devices a virtual stick, run, crouch, view, lamp, throw, jump, and pause buttons appear automatically. The HUD compass points to the nearest live beacon, then back to the lab once all cores are recovered.

## Survival rules

- **Moss.Man is blind.** It hears footsteps, sprinting, hydraulic doors, thrown stones, and core pickups.
- Walking is quiet; sprinting and knuckle-running are loud; crouching reduces your noise and lets you slip past.
- The threat meter shows how close its acoustic map is to you. A roar means it is closing in.
- You cannot outrun it: it reaches 33 km/h and turns at roughly half the agility of a normal pursuer. Break line of sound, crouch, or throw a stone to move its attention.
- Datapads scattered through the lab and jungle contain useful field notes. Medkits restore health.
- Rain, lightning, spores, fireflies, steam, sparks, and dust are all part of the presentation and the atmosphere.

## What is in the build

- Procedural pixel-art textures and flat-shaded voxel/low-poly assets, rendered at a reduced internal resolution with nearest-neighbour scaling.
- Metallic lab lobby with racks, beakers, terminals, hazard markings, animated hydraulic doors, and tactile switches on both sides of every frame.
- Hilly, sparsely forested exterior with beacon sites, ruins, logs, rocks, rain, and dynamic lightning.
- Animated ape player rig with upright walk, quadrupedal sprint, crouch, hill traversal, stamina, headlamp, and two camera modes.
- Fully procedural WebAudio soundscape: wind, rain, electrical hum, footsteps, hydraulic doors, roars, heartbeat, alarms, and UI cues.
- Desktop and mobile HUD, pause/settings, datapad reader, death and win screens.

## Tech

- Static HTML, CSS, and ES modules.
- Vendored [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) r170 and `BufferGeometryUtils`.
- No external art, audio, or network assets; all game content is generated at runtime or stored locally in the repository.

-# PlayGround
+# APE PROJECT — Laboratory Escape
 
-<!-- omgithub:readme:start -->
-## 🚀 Build, play, and remix with OMGithub
+A complete, playable 3D pixel-art survival-horror game that runs in the browser with no build step.
+
+You are the last ape in a failed subterranean research lab. Three isotope cores are scattered across the Mossline jungle outside. Recover them, feed the main terminal, and ride the emergency lift out — while a blind, 2.8 m acoustic apex predator called **Moss.Man** maps the world by sound.
+
+## Play
+
+Open the project through OMGithub, or serve the folder with any static web server and open `index.html`:
+
+```bash
+python3 -m http.server 3000
+# then visit http://localhost:3000/
+```
+
+A local server is required because the game uses ES modules and a vendored Three.js import map.
+
+## Objective
+
+1. Leave the 15 × 15 m lab through one of four hydraulic doors.
+2. Follow the three columns of light to the isotope beacon sites in the 500 × 500 m jungle.
+3. Pick up each core with **E**.
+4. Return to the lab terminal and activate the emergency ascent.
+5. Wait for the shaft to pressurise, then step onto the centre lift pad to escape.
+
+The main terminal stays locked until all three cores are installed. An exterior release switch is mounted to the left of every door frame, so you can always get back inside.
 
-**Created using [OMGithub.com](https://omgithub.com).**
+## Controls
 
-[![OMGithub](https://img.shields.io/badge/OMGithub-Open%20project-orange?style=for-the-badge)](https://omgithub.com/lusialimis-cell/PlayGround)
-[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source-181717?logo=github&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/lusialimis-cell/PlayGround)
+| Action | Keyboard / Mouse |
+| --- | --- |
+| Move | **W A S D** or arrow keys |
+| Look | Move the mouse (click the game to capture the pointer), or drag |
+| Sprint / knuckle-walk | Hold **Shift** |
+| Crouch / quiet movement | **C** (toggle) |
+| Jump | **Space** |
+| Interact / use switch / pick up | **E** |
+| Throw a stone | **Q** |
+| Toggle headlamp | **F** |
+| Toggle first / third person | **V** |
+| Pause | **P** or **Esc** |
+| Toggle audio | **M** |
+| Restart after death or win | **R** |
 
+On touch devices a virtual stick, run, crouch, view, lamp, throw, jump, and pause buttons appear automatically. The HUD compass points to the nearest live beacon, then back to the lab once all cores are recovered.
+
+## Survival rules
+
+- **Moss.Man is blind.** It hears footsteps, sprinting, hydraulic doors, thrown stones, and core pickups.
+- Walking is quiet; sprinting and knuckle-running are loud; crouching reduces your noise and lets you slip past.
+- The threat meter shows how close its acoustic map is to you. A roar means it is closing in.
+- You cannot outrun it: it reaches 33 km/h and turns at roughly half the agility of a normal pursuer. Break line of sound, crouch, or throw a stone to move its attention.
+- Datapads scattered through the lab and jungle contain useful field notes. Medkits restore health.
+- Rain, lightning, spores, fireflies, steam, sparks, and dust are all part of the presentation and the atmosphere.
+
+## What is in the build
+
+- Procedural pixel-art textures and flat-shaded voxel/low-poly assets, rendered at a reduced internal resolution with nearest-neighbour scaling.
+- Metallic lab lobby with racks, beakers, terminals, hazard markings, animated hydraulic doors, and tactile switches on both sides of every frame.
+- Hilly, sparsely forested exterior with beacon sites, ruins, logs, rocks, rain, and dynamic lightning.
+- Animated ape player rig with upright walk, quadrupedal sprint, crouch, hill traversal, stamina, headlamp, and two camera modes.
+- Fully procedural WebAudio soundscape: wind, rain, electrical hum, footsteps, hydraulic doors, roars, heartbeat, alarms, and UI cues.
+- Desktop and mobile HUD, pause/settings, datapad reader, death and win screens.
+
+## Tech
+
+- Static HTML, CSS, and ES modules.
+- Vendored [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) r170 and `BufferGeometryUtils`.
+- No external art, audio, or network assets; all game content is generated at runtime or stored locally in the repository.
